subject: Media Literacy
title: Public vs. Commercial Broadcasting
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Public vs. Commercial Broadcasting.

hook.text: The BBC isn't funded by advertisers. PBS isn't driven by ratings. Their incentives are different — and their journalism shows it.

buildup.text: Public broadcasters are funded by governments or licenses. Commercial broadcasters depend on advertising revenue.

discovery.text: Public media can prioritize public interest over profit. Commercial media must attract audiences to survive financially.

twist.text: Government funding creates its own risk — political pressure to produce favorable coverage of those who control the budget.

climax.text: No funding model is perfect. Each creates different pressures and different blind spots in the journalism produced.

punchline.text: Follow the money. It tells you who the journalism serves.

quiz.question: What risk does government funding pose to public broadcasters?
options: Political pressure to produce favorable coverage of those controlling the budget
No risk — government funding is always neutral
